sections.heading: Roof Repair or Full Replacement? The 25% Rule and NJ Permits

runs.v: A targeted repair makes sense while damage stays at one or two flashing details and the surrounding shingles are sound; minor repairs such as a new pipe boot do not call for a new roof. The 25% rule for roofing says that once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof area, a full replacement usually offers better long-term value than another repair.

Do you need a permit to replace a roof in NJ? Not on a detached one- or two-family home: under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, roof covering repair or replacement there is ordinary maintenance, so minor roof repairs typically need no permit, while on any other building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months requires one. In East Orange, where about 26% of housing units sit in two- to four-unit buildings and about 38% in buildings of 20 or more units (U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019-2023), a detached two-family house is exempt while a three-family walk-up follows the 25% rule.

When replacement is the right call, asphalt shingles are the common choice for residential roof replacements, and roof replacement typically involves high-quality, durable materials; GAF and Owens Corning offer manufacturer warranty options of up to 50 years. New flashing goes on with the new roof.

faqs.q: What is roof flashing and why does it leak on East Orange buildings?

runs.v: Roof flashing is the sheet metal that seals a roof's transitions and penetrations — chimneys, sidewalls, valleys, dormers, and vent stacks. It leaks as the metal corrodes, wind lifts the laps, and sealant cracks, and East Orange's pre-war apartments and converted walk-ups have more of these junctions per roof.

faqs.q: Can you repair flashing without replacing the entire roof on my East Orange building?

runs.v: Yes. Individual flashing details — step flashing at a dormer, counter flashing at a chimney, a pipe-boot replacement at a plumbing vent — are repaired or replaced independently of the primary roof covering.

faqs.q: Does East Orange require a permit for roof flashing repair?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home, where it is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. On multi-family and commercial buildings, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months requires a permit.

faqs.q: Does flashing work on an East Orange historic building need extra approval?

runs.v: National Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof or flashing repair, per the National Park Service. For a listed or locally designated building, confirm with the city whether any local review applies before work begins.

faqs.q: Does caulk fix a flashing leak permanently on my East Orange roof?

runs.v: No. Caulk alone is a temporary flashing repair, because sealant dries and cracks within a few years while properly lapped, corrosion-resistant metal sheds water without relying on the sealant. Where a joint needs sealant, a high-performance sealant backs up the metal rather than replacing it.

faqs.q: How much does roof flashing repair cost in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: A flashing reseal or small flashing section costs $200–$500, per Modernize flashing cost data; a chimney or valley rebuild costs more.

faqs.q: Which flashing metals and roofing materials work best on East Orange homes?

runs.v: Flashings must be selected for the roofing materials they seal: aluminum or galvanized steel with asphalt shingles, copper with slate, and membrane-matched flashing on EPDM, TPO, and modified bitumen. Inspect roof flashing annually so deterioration is caught before it leaks.
